prerequisites: It is highly recommended that the student has passed the second-year course Thermal Engineering.
Assimilated basic knowledge of Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Mathematical Methods taught in the first year.
Knowledge of the main characteristics and fundamental physical laws of the three basic heat transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, and radiation).
Ability to mathematically express equations describing heat transfer problems from fundamental balances (mass, momentum, and heat) and basic heat transfer laws.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Mechanical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Identify variables and results in fluid systems with heat exchange.
Establish relationships between surfaces that exchange heat by radiation in participating media.
Formulate models expressed by differential equations that reproduce a heat transfer problem.
Know and design basic heat exchangers with and without phase change.
Know and energetically evaluate the main heat production equipment and systems.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of convection
Heat exchangers without phase change
Phase change: Boiling. Condensation
Combustion Technology
Heat exchangers with phase change
Radiation in non-participating medium
P1. Convection (Computer)
P2. LMTD method exchanger (Laboratory)
P3. NTU method exchanger (Laboratory)
P4. Boiling and condensation (Computer)
P5. Boiler (Laboratory)
P6. Phase change exchanger (Computer)
P7. Radiation (Computer)
Lesson 1: General conservation equations. Methods for studying convection. Dimensionless numbers. Analysis of main physical convection situations. Use of empirical correlations.
Lesson 2. Forced internal flow convection in pipes. Fully developed flow. Diverse cross-sections. Entrance effects.
Lesson 3. Forced external flow convection. Flat plate. Transverse flow over a cylinder. Flow around a sphere. Natural convection.
Lesson 4: Classification of heat exchangers. Plate heat exchangers. Shell and tube heat exchangers.
Lesson 5: Temperature distribution inside a heat exchanger. Logarithmic mean temperature difference. Overall heat transfer coefficient for flat and finned surfaces.
Lesson 6: Application of the Logarithmic Mean Temperature Difference (L.M.T.D.) method: Data and calculation scheme. Number of Transfer Units (N.T.U.) method: Data and calculation scheme.
Lesson 7. Pool boiling. Nucleate boiling. Maximum heat flux. Film boiling. Minimum heat flux. Flow boiling.
Lesson 8. Laminar film condensation. Turbulent film condensation. Film condensation in horizontal tubes.
Lesson 9. Definitions. Calculation of complete and stoichiometric combustion. Calculation of incomplete combustion and with excess air. Thermal balance in boilers.
Lesson 10. Obtaining temperature versus heat flux diagrams for boiling. Calculation methodology. Capacity ratio. Approach factor for L.M.T.D. application.
Lesson 11. Nature of thermal radiation. Laws of radiation behavior for a black body. Properties of radiation.
Lesson 12. Definition of radiation intensity. Shape factors calculated by integrals. Hottel's method. Algebra of shape factors.
Lesson 13. Radiation balances in non-participating media. Electrical analogy. Particularization of the analogy for a black body and for a re-radiating body.
Lesson 14. Resolution of radiation within enclosures. Radiation exchange between surfaces. Matrix solution method. Radiation shields.
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (reading theoretical foundations, questionnaires, forum participation, additional material viewing)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if the written exam score (EX) is 4 or higher, the course grade is calculated as: NOTE = (0.1 x PA) + (0.10 × PL) + (0.10 × TG) + (0.70 × EX). If the written exam score is less than 4, the course grade is: NOTE = EX. To pass, the course grade must be 5.0 or higher. For extraordinary calls, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 in the written exam (EX) is mandatory to pass. If this minimum is reached, the final grade for the extraordinary call is: NOTE = (0.15 x EP) + (0.85 × EX), where EP is the practical exam. If the student has continuous assessment grades (PA, PL, TG), their average will replace the EP grade.
